blocks.text: Admins can configure content permission sets using specific data attributes that can be assigned to users to specify the data they can access. While role permissions dictate the actions the user can perform (e.g., create a dashboard, merge tickets), content permissions limit the scope of data the user can view and is authorized to perform those actions on. For example, a user might be assigned a role allowing them to create reports, but limited by content permissions, they'll only see data relating to their team (e.g., the team responsible for all Linux assets). To learn more, see Understanding System Roles and Creating Custom Roles.

After content permissions are created, you can assign permission sets to users. When assigned, access changes take effect on the user's next browser refresh. To learn more, see Assigning Content Permissions.
To create a content permission set:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Account Settings.
See image.
In the left-side navigation, go to Permissions > Content.
See image.
On the Content Permissions page, click Create.
See image.
In the Create new permission set drawer:
Name: Enter a name for the permission set.
Type: Select a category for the permission set.
Define filter conditions for the permission set. Conditions define the data included in the permission set (i.e., what data should be included in the user's access).
Select a field that the condition should be based on.
Select an operator (e.g., Equals, Contains). Available operators vary depending on the selected field type.
Enter the value that the rule should apply to.
To apply content permissions to users without manually entering enter unique identifiers, you can add a user's email as a dynamic value.
(Optional) Use AND/OR logic to define compound rules.
AND applies the content permissions to users only if all conditions in the rule are met.
OR applies the content permissions to users if any of the conditions in the rule are met.
See image.
Click Save to create the permission set.

blocks.text: After saving the permission set, you can assign it to users on the User Management page. The newly assigned permission set is applied on the user's next browser refresh. To learn more, see Assigning Content Permissions.

Content permissions only apply to an account's mapped data, so they won't restrict access to unmapped data across the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform). For example, if a user's role grants them access to Logs or Data Mapping, their content permissions won't apply to those resources.

Additionally, content restrictions for scheduled reports and custom dashboard exports conform to the permission set of the user that created the report or the dashboard. The permission set of the receiver is not considered, so the delivered report can include data that the receiver can't access by their own permissions if they are also a user in the system.

blocks.heading: Restricting Manual Override Values with Content Permissions

blocks.text: You can use content permissions with manual content validation to control which values users can select when they manually update a field.

For example, you can allow users to manually update the Verdict field of an Agentic SOC incident. With manual content validation, you can define the approved values users can enter, such as Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious, or True Positive. To learn more about manual content validation, see Adding and Managing Entities and Fields.

You can then configure content permissions to restrict which users can select specific values. For example, you can create a content permission set that only allows security analysts to select Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, or Suspicious.

You can then create another content permission set that only allows senior security analysts or incident responders to select all values. This ensures that manual updates for high-impact values (e.g., Malicious and True Positive) are only available to certain users.

You can grant dynamic access based on the email address of the current user to avoid the need to create a separate condition for each individual user email address. For example, to grant access to all Linux Team users to the tickets assigned to each individual team member, you can add a condition to the Linux Team permission set, select the Assignee Email field, and enter the dynamic {user_email} value.

blocks.item: In the Create new permission set drawer:
Name: Enter a name for the permission set.
Type: Select a category for the permission set.
Define filter conditions for the permission set.
Select the relevant field from the list that contains your users' email address information (e.g., Assignee Email).
Select the Equals operator.
Only the Equals operator is supported, as the field's value should be a unique identifier.
Enter the {user_email} value.
See image.
(Optional) Use AND/OR logic to define compound rules.
AND applies the content permissions to users only if all conditions in the rule are met.
OR applies the content permissions to users if any of the conditions in the rule are met.
Click Save to create the permission set.
